metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent used Ctrl+Shift+T to reopen TripAdvisor tab. Setup had both lonelyplanet.com and airbnb.com open before the task started.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can switch between open tabs; demonstrated knowledge of Chrome tab navigation.
metadata.failure_analysis: Original task failure unrelated to tab switching capability; agent proved it can identify and interact with browser tabs.
metadata.task_rationale: Uses the existing lonelyplanet.com tab (opened by setup) as the target. Tests basic tab-switching capability demonstrated by the agent. Evaluator checks active URL via accessibility tree without page reload.
metadata.explanation: The setup opens lonelyplanet.com as one of the tabs. The task asks the agent to make that tab active. Evaluator reads the active URL from the accessibility tree and checks it matches 'lonelyplanet.com'.

llm_judge_reasons: The getter 'active_url_from_accessTree' correctly extracts the active tab's URL from Chrome's accessibility tree address bar — exactly the right state for verifying which tab is active.
The metric 'is_expected_url_pattern_match' correctly handles the 'type: rule' expected parameter: it receives the rules dict directly and accesses rules['expected'] to get the regex patterns list.
The regex pattern 'lonelyplanet\\.com' correctly matches any lonelyplanet.com URL via re.search, providing appropriate flexibility for URL variations (www prefix, paths, etc.).
The task has a single requirement (active tab must be lonelyplanet.com), and the evaluator fully covers it.

Negative control resistance is satisfied: setup opens tabs in order lonelyplanet.com → airbnb.com → tripadvisor.com, then closes tripadvisor.com, so the initial active tab should be airbnb.com (not lonelyplanet.com), meaning the evaluator would correctly return 0 in the initial state.
